The second document about

Kings

Introduction

The Second King is the continuation of the story about the two kingdom of Israilitas which wasn't finish in the First King. This document is divided into two: 1/ The story about the two kingdom from the middle of the ninth century before Christ was_born until the Samarya was defeated, and it ends when the kingdom there in the north(LIT left side) was finished in the year 722 before Christ was_born. 2/ The story about the kingdom of Huda from the (time when) kingdom of Israil was defeated until the collapse and destruction of Hirusalim by_means_of Nibukadnisar the king of Babilunya in the year 586 before Hisus was_born. The story ends when Gidalya became a governor there in Huda under the ruling of Babilunya, and when King Hihuwakin was released who was imprisoned there in Babilunya.

That destruction, happened in the nation of Israil because the kings and the people of Huda did not obey God (MS Manama). The destruction of Hirusalim and the capturing of the people of Huda is the one considered as big event in the history of Israil.

Prophet Ilisyu was the (one who) was well known in the second King. Ilisyu was the one replaced by Ilyas.

What's_written(pl) in this document (LIT reading)

The divided_up kinging (1:1–17:41)

a. The prophet Ilisyu (1:1–8:15)

b. The kings of Huda and of Israil (8:16–17:4)

c. The defeat of Samarya (17:5-41)

The kinging of Huda (18:1–25:30)

a. From Isikiyas up to Husiyas (18:1–21:26)

b. The kinging by Husiyas (22:1–23:30)

c. The final king of Huda (23:31–24:20)

d. The defeat of Hirusalim (25:1-30)

Gidalyas the governor there in Huda

(Jer 40:7‑9; 41:1‑ 41:1‑3)

22 And Nibukadnisar made Gidalyas as governor of the people who were_left_behind in Huda. He (was) the child of Ahikam the grandchild of Sapan. 23 When all the officers of the soldiers heard that message, they went to Mispa to meet Gidaliyas. They were Ismail the child of Nitaniyas, Diyuhanan the child of Kariyas, Sirayas the child of Tanhumit from_Nitupa, and Hasaniyas from_Maaka with all their men. 24 Then Gidaliyas swore to them saying, “Don't(pl) be_afraid of the officers of the (ones) from_Babilunya. Settle_down(pl) here and be obedient to the king of Babilunya, and no bad_things happen to you(pl).” 25 But in the seventh month in that year, Ismail the child of Nitaniyas who was the grandchild of Ilisama the relative of the king's family, went_there to Mispa together with his ten (10) men in_order to kill Gidaliyas including the Hudiyu and the (ones) from_Babilunya who were with him there. And they indeed killed him. 26 And from that, all the (ones) from_Israil fled to Ihiptu, rich or poor with the officers of the soldiers because they were_afraid that the (ones) from_Babilunya will_revenge them.

The setting_free of Hihuwakin from the prison

(Jer 52:31‑34)

27 In the thirty seventh (37) year that Huwakin the king of Huda was captured, Ibil-Mirudak became the king of Babilunya. In the first year of his kinging, he released Huwakin. It happened on the twenty seventh (27) days of the twelfth (12) month. 28 Huwakin was fair_treated/cared by Ibil-Mirudak, he give (him) a big/high authority than other Kings who_were also captured and were_taken to Babilunya with him. 29 And Huwakin did not wear his prison clothes any_longer, and he ate together with the king daily. 30 And each day while he was still alive, the king of Babilunya gave him everything he needed.
